From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. 11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller SPA Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Preliminary points

- **The "FINAL / not to be re-opened" label is not binding.** The cover note says the positions were "settled at principal level." Before relying on that, confirm with Wattlebridge principals whether any of these points were actually agreed. Several "settled" positions contradict the Seller's own Disclosure Letter:
  - **Bluefen:** the Seller calls it "addressed," but DL §2 says no consent has been obtained.
  - **Riverlark:** the facility is not repaid, and no security discharge is provided (DL §3).
  - **Privacy incident:** the Seller calls it "not expected to be material," but DL §6 says scope, access and notifiability are unknown.
- **The "market context" preamble is advocacy, not evidence.** Some figures are within ordinary ranges for general warranties. That does not justify applying them to title, tax, indemnities or fraud, and the draft tries to do exactly that.
- **The data room cut-off (22 Sept 2026) is about six weeks old.** Require a refreshed disclosure position and a bring-down at Completion.

The figures below are opening and fallback positions for the deal team to calibrate. They are not fixed rules.

---

## SPA-N-001: General liability cap (cl 12.1)
- **Seller:** Aggregate cap of 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims.
- **Buyer wants:** A higher general cap, and confirmation that the cap applies **only** to general warranties. Fundamental, tax, specific indemnities, covenants, leakage and fraud should sit outside it.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 30–40%. 20% is an acceptable fallback, but only if every carve-out in N-004, N-005 and N-014 is secured, or W&I cover tops it up. *Reason: 20% is defensible for general warranties alone, but not as a ceiling on all exposure.*

## SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket (cl 12.2)
- **Seller:** De minimis of AUD 25k, plus a deductible basket of AUD 250k (about 1%), with only the excess recoverable.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A lower de minimis (about AUD 10–15k).
  - Related claims aggregated for de minimis purposes.
  - A **tipping** basket of about 0.5% (AUD 120k) that recovers from the first dollar once exceeded.
  - Neither threshold applying to fundamental, tax, indemnity, covenant or fraud claims.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the deductible structure and counter as above. *Reason: a deductible basket plus a high de minimis can permanently absorb several genuine mid-sized claims.*

## SPA-N-003: General claims time limit (cl 12.3/13)
- **Seller:** 18 months for general claims. Seller also wants any limitation to apply to **all** Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - At least 24 months for general warranties, covering at least one full post-Completion audit.
  - Tax: 7 years, or the statutory amendment period plus 60 days.
  - Fundamental: 7 years.
  - Indemnities: bespoke periods.
  - Proceedings to be issued within 9 months of notice.
  - The default reversed, so limitations apply only where expressly stated.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24 months and reject the "applies to all Claims" default. *Reason: the default would silently cut tax and title claims down to 18 months.*

## SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limits "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** Capacity, authority, title, no encumbrances and share capital treated as fundamental warranties:
  - capped at 100% of price;
  - 7-year survival;
  - no de minimis or basket;
  - no disclosure or knowledge qualifier.
- **Recommendation:** Reject outright. *Reason: the Buyer is paying AUD 24m for the shares, and a defect in title is a total loss that a 20% cap cannot address.*

## SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5)
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature." There is no fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out from all limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions for fraud, dishonesty, wilful misconduct or wilful concealment by the Seller, the Company or their officers and advisers. Non-reliance should also not purport to exclude claims that cannot lawfully be excluded, such as misleading or deceptive conduct under ACL s 18.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Make the carve-out non-negotiable. *Reason: no buyer should accept capped or time-barred recovery for the Seller's own fraud.*

## SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope (Schedule 7; DL §1.1–1.2)
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (as at 22 Sept 2026), the Accounts, statutory registers and all public records.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Specific disclosures only, made **fairly**, with enough detail for the Buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its likely effect.
  - The data room deemed disclosed only to the extent so fairly disclosed.
  - At most, limited public searches (ASIC, PPSR, court searches on stated dates) deemed disclosed.
  - No disclosure against fundamental warranties, tax or specific indemnities.
  - An updated cut-off and a bring-down protocol.
- **Recommendation:** Reject general disclosure. *Reason: it turns the warranties into a document-review exercise and shifts all risk to the Buyer.*

## SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier (cl 8.3)
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter known to the Buyer **or its advisers**, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** An express pro-sandbagging clause, so Buyer knowledge does not limit claims. Fallback: only the **actual** knowledge of named Buyer individuals, and only of matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. *Reason: "discoverable" plus imputed adviser knowledge would wipe out nearly every claim, including the very issues identified in diligence.*

## SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3)
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. DL §2 confirms no consent has been obtained and the cl 11.3 conditions are unsatisfied.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A condition precedent requiring **unconditional** written consent under DD-002 cl 11.2, with all cl 11.3 conditions satisfied, in form and substance satisfactory to the Buyer acting reasonably.
  - No adverse change to Bluefen's terms.
  - All-reasonable-endeavours obligation on the Seller.
  - A waiver right for the Buyer only, a long-stop date and a termination right.
  - Consider a specific indemnity or price protection if Bluefen terminates or reprices within an agreed period.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the Seller's formulation. *Reason: Bluefen is about 30% of revenue (AUD 3.6m), and a bare consent that leaves conditions open does not protect value.*

## SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility (cl 2/7)
- **Seller:** Release "following Completion." About AUD 3.2m is outstanding, there is change-of-control at cl 8.1, and no discharge has been provided (DL §3).
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Repayment **at** Completion from the purchase price under a payoff letter.
  - Executed deed of release and discharge, and PPSR and any mortgage releases, delivered as Completion deliverables.
  - The amount deducted as Debt under the debt-free/cash-free mechanics.
  - A Riverlark waiver of the change-of-control default in the interim.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the post-Completion release. *Reason: the change-of-control trigger hits on Completion, and an undischarged lender is a priority creditor, possibly over the shares themselves (see N-015).*

## SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses (funds flow; DL §5)
- **Seller:** AUD 420k of Completion bonuses described as "a matter for the Seller" and omitted from the funds flow. On-costs are not addressed.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Bonuses plus all on-costs (NSW payroll tax, superannuation guarantee, PAYG withholding, any leave loading) treated as Transaction Costs or Debt and deducted from price.
  - Payment through Company payroll with correct withholding.
  - A specific indemnity for any shortfall or later claims.
  - Clarity on continued-employment conditions and who bears unvested amounts.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the omission. *Reason: the liability sits in the Company, so leaving it out of the funds flow means the Buyer pays for it, plus about 15–20% on-costs, contrary to the cash-free/debt-free basis.*

## SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1)
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "adequate."
- **Buyer wants:**
  - As a condition precedent or Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment of every SOW3 fee (including the AUD 180k shown open in DD-010) and a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay of the SOW3 Project Materials under DD-004 cl 7.3.
  - Indemnity scope extended to **all** loss from the Company not owning or being free to use the SOW3 materials: third-party and Ironquay claims, re-development or licensing costs, and customer claims.
  - The indemnity outside the cap, basket, disclosure and knowledge qualifiers.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. *Reason: until every fee clears, title to the IP does not pass, and the real exposure is the IP, not the AUD 180k.*

## SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6; DL §6)
- **Seller:** "Preliminary" and "not expected to be material." The DL admits access, scope and notifiability are unknown for about 1,240 records.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Pre-Completion covenants: complete the investigation, obtain a forensic or independent report shared with the Buyer, and document a Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Part IIIC eligible-data-breach assessment. Note the 30-day assessment window has likely already passed, which is itself a compliance risk to check. Make any required OAIC or individual notifications.
  - A specific uncapped indemnity, or one capped at a high separate figure, outside basket, disclosure and knowledge qualifiers, surviving at least 3–4 years. It should cover regulator action, penalties to the extent lawful, notification and remediation costs, and customer and third-party claims.
  - Consider a retention or escrow.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the Seller's characterisation. *Reason: the Seller's own disclosure says the facts are unknown, so the risk cannot sit under general warranties that the Seller has already disclosed against.*

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DL §8; DD-008/DD-011)
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k total) are "ordinary course."
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Copies of the documents and an explanation of why one supply was split into three. Check whether this avoided a board, consent or material-contract threshold.
  - Termination and cancellation rights and accrual status.
  - Whether renewal was a restricted act under the interim-conduct covenants.
  - If not genuinely ordinary course: treat as Leakage or a price adjustment, or require the Seller to procure termination. In any event, specific warranties on these contracts.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the "ordinary course" label without evidence. *Reason: related same-amount renewals read together suggest threshold-splitting, and AUD 330k is material against a AUD 250k basket.*

## SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** All limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly excluded (cl 12.3/13, 9.3/12.8/20.5). Tax and IP fall under the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** A limitations schedule with separate regimes, each with its own cap, time limit and threshold treatment:

  | Category | Cap | Survival | Thresholds | Disclosure/knowledge |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | General warranties | per N-001 | per N-003 | per N-002 | per N-006/007 |
  | Fundamental | 100% | 7 yrs | None | None |
  | Tax (warranties and indemnity) | 100% | 7 yrs or statutory + 60 days | None | None |
  | Specific indemnities (Ironquay, privacy, bonuses, Bluefen/Riverlark as applicable) | Bespoke/100% | Bespoke | None | None |
  | Covenants/leakage | 100% | Bespoke | None | n/a |
  | Fraud | Unlimited | Unlimited | None | None |

  Specific indemnities should not be reduced by disclosure or knowledge.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the single regime. *Reason: one cap, one time limit and blanket disclosure collapse every protection into the weakest one.*

## SPA-N-015: Title verification (DL §10; DD-012)
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the share register at DD-012. The DL itself notes the Buyer has not verified it.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Reconcile the register against current ASIC records, the constitution, share certificates and all issue and transfer history.
  - Confirm there are no options, convertibles, ESOP or phantom equity. The DD-005 bonuses suggest you should check for equity-linked promises.
  - Run a PPSR search, especially for any Riverlark security over the shares.
  - Fundamental title warranty, per N-004.
  - Completion deliverables: executed transfers, original certificates, register update, and releases of any share security.
- **Recommendation:** Do not rely on the register alone. *Reason: a register is internal evidence only, and the Riverlark security may encumber the very shares being sold.*

## SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Tax:** a standalone tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax, including payroll tax and super on the bonuses and any R&D incentive clawback. Cap at 100%, survival per the statutory period, with Seller conduct-of-claims rights balanced by Buyer control.
  - **IP:** expanded IP warranties covering ownership, employee and contractor assignments, open-source use and non-infringement. Higher cap (or fundamental-style treatment for ownership of core IP) and longer survival, with the Ironquay indemnity per N-011.
- **Recommendation:** Treat both as **open**, not settled. *Reason: for a SaaS target, IP ownership and tax are core value drivers and need their own regimes.*

---

## Priority and next steps
1. **Walk-away level issues:** fraud carve-out (N-005), fundamental/title (N-004/N-015), Riverlark at Completion (N-009), Bluefen as a proper condition precedent (N-008), category separation (N-014).
2. **Price-affecting items:** bonuses plus on-costs (N-010), Riverlark debt (N-009), Sandbar (N-013). Re-run the funds flow from AUD 24m on a debt-free/cash-free basis.
3. **Specific indemnities:** Ironquay (N-011), privacy incident (N-012), tax (N-016).
4. **Also check:** the lease notification (DD-007) and Mossvale assignment restriction (DD-009). Confirm neither is triggered by a share sale, though the Seller's "does not state" wording is not a warranty. Require a specific warranty that no other change-of-control consents are needed.
5. **Process:** confirm with Wattlebridge principals whether anything was actually agreed at principal level before responding to the "FINAL" assertion.

I can turn this into a mark-up of cl 8.3, 12 and 13 and a revised limitations schedule, or a short covering response to Seller counsel, if useful.
